text: In the study of Physarum polycephalum, the term 'plasmodium' refers to which life stage?
choices: A colony of genetically distinct amoebae cooperating through chemical signals
A dormant, thick-walled spore capable of surviving for years
A single continuous membrane enclosing a common cytoplasm shared by thousands to millions of nuclei
A multicellular body in which each nucleus is walled off inside its own cell
explanation: The plasmodium is the multinucleate, single-membrane feeding and problem-solving stage: millions of nuclei share one continuous cytoplasm, so it is neither a conventional single cell nor a true multicellular organism. It is not a colony of distinct cells (choice 0) nor a walled multicellular body (choice 3), and the spore (choice 1) is a separate dormant stage of the life cycle.
